headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: plano’s OpenAI-compatible egress can transmit shared content, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress but no direct I/O surfaces documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented. However, plano exposes file input via config.yaml and an OpenAI-compatible API, while awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing/listing agent with broad network egress, so a manual copy-paste or shared-file bridge could carry injected instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies plano-generated text into awesome-cli-apps prompts or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste handoff for untrusted text
Add a prompt-injection warning banner to pasted content
Review any shared config.yaml before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: plano explicitly sends requests to an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint and touches logs/metrics/traces, so shared content can leave the local boundary. awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress, but its profile does not document a specific data sink; uncertainty therefore pushes this to medium rather than low. The pair can leak workspace content if they share files or prompts.
conditions: IF both agents read the same file or prompt buffer
IF plano forwards user content to its chat-completions backend
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in shared files
Rotate any credentials present in shared configs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but only plano documents an API call surface and config file; awesome-cli-apps has no write surfaces or mutable shared resource access documented. There is no evidence of overlapping filesystem, git, or OAuth writes, so conflict is limited to unusual shared-resource setups.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or shared file
IF an orchestrator gives them the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: requires-engineering: add resource locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: plano can act as an AI gateway and emit routed outputs, while awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing agent that may consume those outputs as text. If one agent’s generated content is treated as authoritative by the other, errors can cascade into downstream writing or routing decisions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF awesome-cli-apps uses plano-generated text as source material without verification
IF plano routes or rewrites content that awesome-cli-apps then republishes
mitigations: Add a verification step for all routed outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source docs-only entries. The only concrete compliance-relevant signal is plano’s logs/metrics/traces handling, which could matter if sensitive data is introduced, but the pairwise compliance breach is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through plano’s logging or API path
IF the operator requires a residency or retention guarantee not documented in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
